caption:
5 deaths and 1,110 hospitalizations in just 24 hours. Dengue continues to surge across Bangladesh.

Five people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll for the year to 107, according to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Wednesday.

A total of 1,110 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country in the last 24 hours.

The regional breakdown of hospitalizations shows Dhaka division leading with 440 patients, followed by Chattogram with 175, Khulna with 190, and Barishal with 110.

Other affected areas include Rajshahi with 91, Mymensingh with 65, Rangpur with 32, and Sylhet with 7 patients.

This latest surge brings the total number of dengue patients treated in hospitals this year to 38,280.

headline: LPG price cut by Tk 13, 12kg cylinder now Tk 1,585
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission has reduced the price of liquefied petroleum gas for September, bringing some relief to consumers.
details: The price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has been reduced by Tk 13 for September, bringing the cost of a 12kg cylinder down to Tk 1,585 from Tk 1,598.
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced the new price, which takes effect from 6:00pm today.
Despite the cut, the price remains Tk 57 higher than it was in July, when a 12kg cylinder was sold at Tk 1,528, following a Tk 70 increase in August.
According to BERC, the new local rate was fixed based on the average Saudi Contract Price (CP) for September, which stood at $647.75 per tonne.
The commission's calculation also took into account freight charges, traders' premiums, and an average exchange rate of Tk 123.30 per US dollar.
Additionally, the price of autogas used in vehicles has been reduced to Tk 73.09 per litre.
caption:
LPG prices are down! A 12kg cylinder now costs Tk 1,585.

The price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has been reduced by Tk 13 for September, bringing the cost of a 12kg cylinder down to Tk 1,585 from Tk 1,598.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced the new price, which takes effect from 6:00pm today.

Despite the cut, the price remains Tk 57 higher than it was in July, when a 12kg cylinder was sold at Tk 1,528, following a Tk 70 increase in August.

According to BERC, the new local rate was fixed based on the average Saudi Contract Price (CP) for September, which stood at $647.75 per tonne.

The commission's calculation also took into account freight charges, traders' premiums, and an average exchange rate of Tk 123.30 per US dollar.

Additionally, the price of autogas used in vehicles has been reduced to Tk 73.09 per litre.

Source: Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
